articles.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
articles.description: NASA has revealed an accelerated plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing competing lunar landers and a crucial orbital test scheduled for 2027. Faster rocket preparations, new lightweight spacesuits, and redesigned missions could help pave the way for a permanent lunar presence and future human exploration of Mars.
articles.summary: NASA has announced an accelerated plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing lunar landers. This bold initiative marks a historic milestone in human space exploration and lunar return efforts.

articles.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
articles.description: New research suggests that Little Red Dots, which have puzzled astronomers since the JWST began discovering them, could host primordial black holes born during the Big Bang.
articles.summary: New research suggests the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots could be primordial black holes from the Big Bang era, potentially unlocking secrets of the universe's earliest moments. This groundbreaking discovery revolutionizes our understanding of black hole origins.

articles.title: NASA unveils $10B Moon base contract as SpaceX, Blue Origin join lunar gold rush
articles.description: NASA announced Saturday that Elon Musk’s SpaceX, Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin and six other aerospace companies are eligible to compete for up to $10 billion in lunar delivery contracts as the agency advances plans to establish a permanent base on the moon. The an…
articles.summary: NASA awards a $10 billion Moon base contract to SpaceX, Blue Origin, and six other aerospace companies, accelerating humanity's return to the lunar surface and establishing a permanent lunar presence.

articles.title: Rubies on Mars?
articles.description: Written by Roger C. Wiens, SuperCam Principal Investigator for NASA’s Perseverance rover at Purdue University Nov. 4, 2026 Exploration on Mars turns up the unexpected. Perseverance is equipped with a fantastic set of instruments for studying the rock record of this ancient planet. Both PIXL and SuperCam have great capabilities for detecting all kinds of […]
articles.summary: Perseverance rover's SuperCam discovers evidence of ruby-like minerals on Mars. This unexpected finding expands our understanding of Mars' mineral diversity and geological history.

articles.title: Newest Sample, Oldest Rock?
articles.description: Written by Tasha Coelho, Mastcam-Z Student Collaborator at Arizona State University Nov. 1, 2026 Perseverance’s most recent abrasion “Pumbe” bears a striking resemblance to an earlier abrasion, “Badger Peak.” That’s no coincidence. As previously reported, that rock had a hardness too high to core. However, the team felt strongly that it was worth the effort […]
articles.summary: Perseverance rover collects its oldest rock sample yet discovered on Mars. This ancient specimen provides crucial insights into Mars' early geological history.

articles.title: NASA’s Chandra Finds Source of Star’s Mysterious Outbursts
articles.description: Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what is triggering repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star. A new study, published Monday in the latest issue of The Astrophysical Journal, details the discovery of a previously hidden companion object that keeps pulling material away from the massive star every 113 days as they orbit […]
articles.summary: NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory identifies the source of mysterious stellar outbursts from a giant star. This discovery enhances our understanding of stellar behavior and dynamics.

articles.title: Simulations cast doubt on unusual asteroid's 'dark comet' status
articles.description: In 2031, Japan's Hayabusa2 spacecraft will arrive at the near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26: a tiny body that is accelerating in a way that astronomers have struggled to explain. Some studies have suggested that the asteroid is pushed along by water escaping from it as gas, making it an as-yet theoretical "dark comet."
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Japan's Hayabusa2 spacecraft will investigate near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26 in 2031, with new simulations clarifying the nature of this unusual celestial body. The mission promises groundbreaking data about small asteroids and their properties.

articles.title: The ELT can probe ultra-diffuse galaxies and their dark matter mysteries
articles.description: We've been waiting a long time for the Extremely Large Telescope's first light, scheduled for March 2029. Telescopes this large, powerful and costly always have multiple science goals, and that's true for the ELT. One of its science goals is to study fundamental aspects of the universe, including dark matter.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The Extremely Large Telescope's first light in March 2029 will unlock mysteries of ultra-diffuse galaxies and dark matter through unprecedented observational power. This revolutionary instrument represents a major leap in astronomical capability.

articles.title: First known 'disappearing planet' has a neighbor that makes it wobble like a top
articles.description: UCLA-led astronomers have discovered the first known "disappearing planet" about 1,000 light-years away. The planet, TOI-2535 b, is a "hot Jupiter," a gas giant that orbits extremely close to its host star. TOI-2535 b whips around its star in only 8.25 days—10 times faster than the 88 days that Mercury takes to go around our sun once.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: UCLA-led astronomers have discovered the first known 'disappearing planet' 1,000 light-years away, along with a companion planet creating fascinating gravitational interactions. This remarkable finding opens new avenues for studying planetary behavior.

articles.title: Caltech robot makes history by building a structure in space
articles.description: For the first time, a robot has autonomously built part of a structure in space, demonstrating a breakthrough that could fundamentally change space exploration. The technology could one day allow scientists to construct enormous telescopes, communications antennas, and solar power stations in orbit, far beyond the size limits of today's rockets.
articles.summary: A Caltech-developed robot has made history by autonomously building a structure in space, demonstrating breakthrough capabilities for future construction missions. This achievement paves the way for revolutionary in-space manufacturing and assembly technologies.

articles.title: Mysterious gas leaks suggest Mars may still be volcanically alive
articles.description: Mysterious gas emissions and fresh volcanic fissures suggest that Mars may not be geologically dead after all, with hot magma potentially still active deep underground. The discovery could point to hidden pockets of warmth and chemical energy capable of supporting microbial life beneath the Red Planet’s surface.
articles.summary: Mysterious gas emissions and fresh volcanic fissures suggest Mars may still harbor active volcanic processes, challenging previous assumptions about the planet's geological status. This discovery opens exciting possibilities for understanding Mars's dynamic interior.

articles.title: Einstein's equations reveal how gravity could break, reconnect, and release energy
articles.description: More than a century after Einstein revolutionized our understanding of gravity, scientists have uncovered a surprising new phenomenon hidden within his equations. Researchers at Columbia University and Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez have identified a theoretical process called "gravitational reconnection," in which structures within gravitational fields can break apart and reconnect, transferring energy into matter.
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered surprising new insights into gravity through Einstein's equations, revealing how gravitational fields could break and reconnect while releasing energy. This theoretical breakthrough expands our fundamental understanding of the universe's most dominant force.

articles.title: NASA is racing against time to save the Hubble Space Telescope
articles.description: NASA is exploring a daring plan to save the legendary Hubble Space Telescope from its eventual fiery plunge into Earth's atmosphere. After more than 35 years of groundbreaking discoveries, Hubble is slowly losing altitude, and without intervention, it could fall back to Earth as early as 2033 or 2034. To keep the iconic observatory operating, NASA is asking private space companies to propose innovative ways to boost Hubble into a higher orbit, upgrade its capabilities, or safely dispose of it when its mission finally ends.
articles.summary: NASA is developing an innovative plan to extend Hubble Space Telescope's operational life and prevent its eventual re-entry into Earth's atmosphere. This daring rescue mission represents a triumph of human ingenuity to preserve one of astronomy's most iconic instruments.

articles.title: NASA's twin ESCAPADE Mars probes slingshot around Earth in unprecedented double 'gravity assist'
articles.description: NASA's twin ESCAPADE spacecraft are wrapping up a year-long voyage to Mars, and are now ready to make a beeline to the Red Planet.
articles.summary: NASA's twin ESCAPADE spacecraft execute an unprecedented double gravity assist maneuver around Earth on their way to Mars. This innovative trajectory demonstrates cutting-edge mission planning for the Red Planet exploration.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
articles.description: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
articles.summary: On November 9, 1967, NASA successfully launched the Saturn V rocket for the first time during the uncrewed Apollo 4 mission. This historic test paved the way for humanity's greatest achievement: landing astronauts on the Moon.

articles.title: NASA opens applications for astronauts who will live on the Moon
articles.description: If you ever wanted to earn a solid wage by living and working on another world, now's your chance. NASA has put out a call for a new generation of ast...
articles.summary: NASA opens applications for astronauts selected to live and work on the Moon, representing humanity's next giant leap in space exploration. This historic opportunity invites qualified candidates to participate in establishing a permanent lunar presence.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists achieve a major breakthrough after a 42-year search, discovering evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay occurring only once per 10 billion events. This landmark finding advances fundamental physics and deepens our understanding of subatomic matter.

articles.title: Step inside the zeptoverse: British scientists use the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside a minuscule world where exotic particles may be hiding
articles.description: British scientists have used the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside the minuscule world of the zeptoverse.
articles.summary: British scientists use the Large Hadron Collider to explore the zeptoverse, the minuscule subatomic realm where exotic particles may exist. This cutting-edge research peers deeper into nature's fundamental building blocks than ever before.

articles.title: The Vera Rubin Has Found Two More of the Milky Way's Dim Satellites
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory has detected two more of the Milky Ways' dim, hard to see satellites. One is an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy, and one is a globular cluster. Each one is a missing piece of the puzzle in the Milky Way's merger history. By finding more of…
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory has discovered two additional ultra-faint satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, advancing our understanding of galactic structure and dark matter distribution.

articles.summary: New research uses nanohertz gravitational-wave observations to constrain the properties of supermassive binary black holes formed in the early universe, opening new avenues for studying cosmic evolution.

articles.title: Researchers May Have Discovered the 6th Dwarf Planet
articles.description: The other five are Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake.
articles.summary: Researchers have potentially identified a sixth dwarf planet in our solar system, expanding our catalog of these distant icy worlds beyond the well-known five.

articles.title: Want to fly to moon? NASA is looking for new astronauts to help grow its Artemis programme
articles.description: Want to fly to the moon and help build a permanent lunar base? NASA is accepting applications for a new astronaut class that will help grow the Artemis programme.
articles.summary: NASA is recruiting new astronauts for the Artemis program, offering opportunities to participate in lunar missions and contribute to establishing a permanent Moon base.

articles.summary: NASA announces new awards and mission updates for Moon Base exploration projects, advancing scientific research and technology development for sustained lunar operations.

articles.summary: Curiosity rover achieves its 49th successful drill hole at the Nazca site on Mars. This milestone reveals new mineralogical data about Mars' geological composition.

articles.summary: NASA recruits the next generation of astronauts to lead humanity's future space exploration missions. The agency seeks innovative explorers to write the next chapter of space discovery.

articles.title: Tiny Solar Whirlpools May Hold the Secret to the Sun’s Blistering Corona
articles.description: For the second time in a few weeks, we’re writing about research into the temperature gap between the Sun’s surface and its corona. More and more data from various missions continue to feed this wave of discovery. A new paper by Katariina Nykyri of Embry-Riddle, recently published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, adds to this growing body of work. She argues that millions of tiny whirlpools scattered across the Sun’s surface could be the energetic engine driving that temperature difference.
articles.summary: Researchers discover that tiny solar whirlpools may explain the Sun's scorching corona temperature anomaly. This breakthrough advances solar physics and our understanding of stellar atmospheres.

articles.title: Using Vibrations and AI, Future Robotic Missions Could Handle Buried Rocks Autonomously
articles.description: Mechanical engineering assistant professor Erik Komendera developed a method that combines vibrations and AI to determine how deeply a rock is buried, helping robots clear terrain more efficiently.
articles.summary: Innovative AI and vibration technology enable future robotic missions to autonomously handle buried rocks on alien worlds. This advancement promises enhanced capabilities for robotic space exploration.

articles.title: Mars' Molten Heart is Long Gone, but Some Magma Chambers May Persist
articles.description: Mars may be more volcanically active than we thought, according to new research. The Trace Gas Orbiter detected HCl, a chemical associated with magma, at a time of year that's difficult except by volcanic origins. The new research also identified new surface fissures on Mars that could be the source of the chemical.
articles.summary: Research reveals that Mars may retain active magma chambers despite its cooled core. This discovery suggests Mars retains more geological activity than previously believed.
